info.title: Assets
info.description: Use the assets endpoint to upload images and files to Content Lake and to link Media Library assets to a dataset.

post.description:
Upload an image asset to Content Lake.
This uploads an image and creates a linked `sanity.imageAsset` document containing the image metadata.

400.description: Invalid request, such as a parameter that fails validation, an empty body, an unsupported image type (`Unsupported image type`), or an image whose metadata can't be read.

401.description: Unauthorized. The token is missing a valid session, for example `Session not found`.

402.description: Payment required. A usage limit blocks asset uploads for this project. The response body's `error` and `message` fields give the reason.

403.description: Forbidden. The request has no token, or the token lacks the `create` permission in the dataset. The body is a `mutationError` with an `insufficientPermissionsError` item.

422.description: The image could not be processed. The message is `Invalid image, could not process`.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded for writes to this asset, with the message `Rate limit exceeded for mutations to this asset`. This happens when the same file is uploaded repeatedly in a short time. Wait before uploading it again.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, for example because of a storage rate limit or an image processing timeout. Try again.

post.description:
Upload a file asset to Content Lake.
This uploads a file and creates a linked `sanity.fileAsset` document containing the file metadata.
The asset's `mimeType` is taken from the request's `Content-Type` header. Set `filename` to keep the original extension.

400.description: Invalid request, such as a parameter that fails validation or an empty body.

401.description: Unauthorized. The token is missing a valid session, for example `Session not found`.

402.description: Payment required. A usage limit blocks asset uploads for this project. The response body's `error` and `message` fields give the reason.

403.description: Forbidden. The request has no token, or the token lacks the `create` permission in the dataset. The body is a `mutationError` with an `insufficientPermissionsError` item.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded for writes to this asset, with the message `Rate limit exceeded for mutations to this asset`. This happens when the same file is uploaded repeatedly in a short time. Wait before uploading it again.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, for example because of a storage rate limit or an image processing timeout. Try again.

post.summary: Upload an image asset from a URL
post.description:
Upload an image asset from a public or preauthorized HTTPS URL and create a `sanity.imageAsset` document in Content Lake.

Sanity fetches the source without forwarding your API token, cookies, or request headers. The source and each redirect destination must use HTTPS without embedded credentials and pass the source policy. Up to three redirects are followed. The source is limited to 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes), and fetching may take up to 300 seconds. The JSON request body is limited to 4 KiB.

Provide `filename` in the JSON body; the `filename` query parameter is not accepted. The other upload metadata parameters work as on the ordinary upload endpoint. Provide `sourceName` and `sourceId` together; `sourceUrl` is attribution metadata, not the URL to fetch.

Allow more than 300 seconds for the client request. If the connection closes or the request times out, check the dataset before retrying: the asset may already have been created. Use the returned `document._id` as the asset reference in an image or file field.

parameters.name: meta
parameters.description: Image metadata to extract. Repeat the parameter for multiple values, such as meta=palette&meta=lqip.

400.description: Invalid request or source URL, blocked destination, redirect limit exceeded, empty or unsupported source content, or the source returned a 4xx status other than 408, 425, or 429. Check that the URL returns asset bytes without additional authentication.

401.description: Unauthorized. Also returned with the message `Session expires too soon for asset URL ingestion. Please retry.` when the session for the request expires in less than 390 seconds.

402.description: Payment required. A usage limit blocks asset uploads for this project. The response body's `error` and `message` fields give the reason.

403.description: Forbidden. The request has no token, or the token lacks the `create` permission in the dataset. The body is a `mutationError` with an `insufficientPermissionsError` item.

413.description: Source exceeds 50 MiB or the JSON request body exceeds 4 KiB.

422.description: The image could not be processed. The message is `Invalid image, could not process`.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded for writes to this asset, with the message `Rate limit exceeded for mutations to this asset`. This happens when the same file is uploaded repeatedly in a short time. Wait before uploading it again.

502.description: Source could not be fetched, or returned a server error or a transient status (408, 425, or 429). Check that the URL is reachable and try again.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, for example because of a storage rate limit or an image processing timeout. Try again.

504.description: Source fetch or gateway request timed out. Check the dataset before retrying.

post.summary: Upload a file asset from a URL
post.description:
Upload a file asset from a public or preauthorized HTTPS URL and create a `sanity.fileAsset` document in Content Lake.

The source's `Content-Type` header is not used. The asset's `mimeType` and extension come from `filename` or from the file content, so provide `filename` to get the right type.

Sanity fetches the source without forwarding your API token, cookies, or request headers. The source and each redirect destination must use HTTPS without embedded credentials and pass the source policy. Up to three redirects are followed. The source is limited to 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes), and fetching may take up to 300 seconds. The JSON request body is limited to 4 KiB.

Provide `filename` in the JSON body; the `filename` query parameter is not accepted. The other upload metadata parameters work as on the ordinary upload endpoint. Provide `sourceName` and `sourceId` together; `sourceUrl` is attribution metadata, not the URL to fetch.

Allow more than 300 seconds for the client request. If the connection closes or the request times out, check the dataset before retrying: the asset may already have been created. Use the returned `document._id` as the asset reference in an image or file field.

400.description: Invalid request or source URL, blocked destination, redirect limit exceeded, empty or unsupported source content, or the source returned a 4xx status other than 408, 425, or 429. Check that the URL returns asset bytes without additional authentication.

401.description: Unauthorized. Also returned with the message `Session expires too soon for asset URL ingestion. Please retry.` when the session for the request expires in less than 390 seconds.

402.description: Payment required. A usage limit blocks asset uploads for this project. The response body's `error` and `message` fields give the reason.

403.description: Forbidden. The request has no token, or the token lacks the `create` permission in the dataset. The body is a `mutationError` with an `insufficientPermissionsError` item.

413.description: Source exceeds 50 MiB or the JSON request body exceeds 4 KiB.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded for writes to this asset, with the message `Rate limit exceeded for mutations to this asset`. This happens when the same file is uploaded repeatedly in a short time. Wait before uploading it again.

502.description: Source could not be fetched, or returned a server error or a transient status (408, 425, or 429). Check that the URL is reachable and try again.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, for example because of a storage rate limit or an image processing timeout. Try again.

504.description: Source fetch or gateway request timed out. Check the dataset before retrying.

post.summary: Link a Media Library asset to a dataset
post.description:
Creates a linked Media Library asset in your dataset. To support features like preview,
Media Library assets need to be linked to a local asset document.
Pair with the [Mutation API](https://www.sanity.io/docs/http-reference/mutation) to attach linked Media Library assets to documents.
Requires a token for a Sanity user. Robot tokens are rejected.

parameters.name: meta
parameters.description: Image metadata to copy from the Media Library asset to the linked asset document. Applies to image assets only. `dimensions`, `hasAlpha`, and `isOpaque` are always included. Repeat the parameter for multiple values, such as meta=palette&meta=lqip.

assetId.description:
The asset ID of the Media Library asset. This comes from the `asset._id` field
returned as part of the response when uploading an asset to the library.

mediaLibraryId.description: The ID of the Media Library.

assetInstanceId.description:
The asset instance ID of the Media Library asset. This comes from the `assetInstance._id` field
returned as part of the response when uploading an asset to the library.

document.description: The linked asset document in your dataset. Its `_type` is `sanity.imageAsset`, `sanity.fileAsset`, or `sanity.videoAsset`.

401.description: Unauthorized. Also returned with the message `Invalid non-global session for user id <id>` when the request uses a robot token.

403.description: Forbidden. The message is `Could not access media library asset` when you can't read the asset in the Media Library. Also returned when the token lacks the `create` permission in the dataset.

404.description: The Media Library asset was not found. The message starts with `Asset not found`, or is `Media library asset not found` when the stored file is missing.

422.description: The Media Library asset can't be linked. The message is `Media library asset is not ready` for a video that is still processing, or `Asset instance does not belong to asset container` when `assetInstanceId` doesn't belong to `assetId`.

tagParam.name: tag
tagParam.description: Optional request tag for the upload. Learn more in the [request tag documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/platform-management/reference-api-request-tags).

MetaParam.name: meta
MetaParam.description: Array of metadata to extract from asset

labelParam.name: label
labelParam.description: Optional freeform label for the asset.

creditLineParam.name: creditLine
creditLineParam.description: The credit to people or organizations required by the supplier of the asset to be used when published.

sourceNameParam.name: sourceName
sourceNameParam.description: The name of the source if the asset is from an external service. Requires `sourceId`.

sourceIdParam.name: sourceId
sourceIdParam.description: The ID of the asset within the external source. Required when `sourceName` is set, and ignored without it.

sourceUrlParam.name: sourceUrl
sourceUrlParam.description: The URL of the asset within the external source. Ignored without `sourceName`.

url.description: Public or preauthorized HTTPS URL returning the asset bytes. URLs with embedded usernames or passwords are not supported.

filename.description: Optional original filename, including the extension. Must not contain path separators or a null character.

url.description: The CDN URL of the asset

size.description: Size of the asset in bytes.

metadata.description: Metadata extracted from the asset. Learn more in the [metadata documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/apis-and-sdks/image-metadata).
